thread:
sam: quick idea — propose we try a "softslot" affinity for embeddings ingress to reduce cross-shard routing churn. short version: route by tenant softslot hint but allow fallback to any shard when capacity needed.

julia: sounds interesting. can you sketch the scoring? is this a deterministic mapping or probabilistic?

sam: deterministic primary->softslot hash, but each request carries a `X-Softslot` header optional. runtime will try primary first for low-latency SLOs, else will fallback after timeout/backpressure.

kai: how do we handle quotas & accounting? if we bias one shard we might exhaust tenant quota there and throttle other tenants unfairly.

sam: good catch. plan is: softslot is affinity only, accounting still global across shards (per-tenant tokens consumed). we keep rate-limiter at proxy-level and emit a `route_affinity` tag in telemetry.

maria: what about batch packing? embeddings batching needs similar dims; will softslot increase small-batch fragmentation?

sam: we’ll let the runtime maintain a small pro-active rebalancer: if primary queue is empty for 100ms, route to secondary preferred shard to coalesce. threshold tunable.

zach: write out the fallback policy pls — is it sync or async? we need to avoid extra hops on the critical path.

sam: fallback is sync but cheap: proxy has local cached table of compatible secondary shards. flow: try primary, wait up to `t_primary` ms (config default 15ms), if no capacity, re-route to best secondary (based on free_slots score).

julia: can we add a circuit breaker metric to avoid oscillation? e.g., `route_mig_rate{tenant}` and auto-relax affinity for noisy tenants.

sam: yes — will add `route_mig_rate` + `affinity_hold_count` tags. console will show a per-tenant affinity health sparkline.

maria: telemetry needs to capture: latency_p50/p95/p99 per (tenant, shard, affinity_state), plus `split_rate` and `batch_fill_pct`. otherwise ops can't diagnose fragmentation.

sam: agreed — provisional list: `route_affinity_state`, `route_mig_rate`, `batch_fill_pct`, `latency_by_affinity`, `quota_exhausted_count`. i'll add them to the telemetry PR.

zach: rollout plan suggestion: A) internal canary (dev tenants) 5% traffic w/ affinity on B) 25% with console toggles per org C) global. Add kill-switch to disable affinity per shard.

julia: console UX: add an affordance on tenant page showing "Affinity: ON/OFF", last-mig events, and a top-line cost delta estimate (affinity can reduce cross-shard loads => lower inter-shard network ops).

sam: will prototype UI with a column `affinity_win_rate` and a small help tooltip (why it helps and when to disable).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: `embed-affinity-proto` -> staging at 1763680000

kai: action items: 1) sam: telemetry PR + proto config (deadline EOD Fri) 2) julia: console mockups (next Wed) 3) ops: define rollback SLOs and create grafana/alert for `route_mig_rate` spike.

sam: noted. i'll post the telemetry schema and example spans in this thread. starting with: ```json
{
  "route_affinity_state": "primary|fallback|disabled",
  "route_mig_rate": 0.02,
  "batch_fill_pct": 0.78
}
```

maria: tiny nit — include `requested_dims` and `actual_batch_shape` in traces for embed debugging.

sam: will add. thanks! :thumbsup:

julia: one more: ensure quota logs include `affinity_hint_used` boolean so billing/usage shows it was routed by affinity.

sam: yep. adding `affinity_hint_used` to usage events.

zach: good thread. if staging looks stable let's schedule a 5% canary next Tue and loop in cs/support for potential customer noise.

sam: plan posted. will follow up with PR links and a console mock.
